memory_candidates.content: When a plan names an exact grep/footprint hypothesis for a de-falsification task ('N files, M statements'), re-running that grep before editing can surface a materially larger real footprint (observed: 3 files hypothesized, 5 files + 2 undiscovered script-comment sites found). The plan's own Scope Hypothesis instruction ('report the count rather than silently expand') is the right discipline: fix every site the regrep finds (same falsehood, same acceptance criterion), but record the expanded count explicitly in the commit message and progress-file deviations rather than quietly absorbing it.

A temp-sync-for-testing procedure that copies source-store files into a gitignored deploy tree (.claude/) for test execution, then restores them, MUST restore from the pre-task commit SHA captured before any work began -- not from 'HEAD' read after intermediate phase commits have landed, since HEAD moves forward as work is committed. Restoring from current HEAD mid-task silently hand-deploys the task's own in-progress edits into the deploy tree, violating the source-store-deploy-boundary contract. Capture the starting commit SHA explicitly at the start of any multi-phase task that will need this pattern more than once.

When a lib file's parallel-array class member count changes (e.g. 19->20 in runtime-file-patterns.sh), a test suite that hardcodes the OLD count as a pass/fail assertion (not just an array-length-equality check) will legitimately fail after an otherwise-correct addition. This is a 4th class of 'verbatim carrier' beyond the usual gitignore-pattern-block carriers, found only by actually running the test after the edit, not by grep alone.
